newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian communists propose new policy body.
newsitem.headline: Russian communists propose new policy body.

text.p: Communist leader Gennady Zyuganov, speaking at the start of the autumn session of parliament, proposed a new grouping of political leaders to examine Russia's problems and decide what had to be done.

Zyuganov, accusing the government of being unable to resolve key issues, said his new body should include members of both houses of parliament, government leaders and representatives from the Defence and Security Councils.
The grouping should "immediately look at questions about the situation in the country and formulate basic demands", he said.
"If things go on like this Russia will repeat the fate of the Soviet Union," Zyuganov added. "The government is unable to resolve a single question."
Zyuganov, runner-up to Boris Yeltsin in Russia's presidential election this summer, has said that Yeltsin should step down because his illness.
The president has been in hospital for over two weeks while doctors prepare him for open heart surgery.

The communists are the largest single party in the State Duma lower house of parliament and are hoping that a string of elections for regional governors will give them a strong position in the Federation Council, the upper house.

One communist-backed candidate was elected at the weekend in the Leningrad region surrounding Russia's second city of St Petersburg, but an election in the vast southern region of Rostov returned a reformist governor.
Wednesday's Duma session was opened by parliamentary speaker Gennady Seleznyov.
"Our citizens, quite justifiably, protest against the practice which has grown in recent years of them not receiving the wages they have earned," said Seleznyov, also a communist.
"There is a serious financial crisis, not just in separate branches of industry...but in key state institutions such as the army, law enforcement, education, science and health."
